title: Shadow Cohort Fidelity Stitching Protocol
author: Marco Chen
content:
Summary
--------
This document defines the Shadow Cohort Fidelity Stitching Protocol: an experiment and analysis pattern for running mirrored (shadowed) production traffic across multiple runtime cohorts to validate fidelity, kernel-scheduling and quantization impacts, and end-to-end user-visible regression risk before rollout. The protocol is designed for validating changes that affect execution kernels, scheduler policies, KV cache behavior, quantization profiles, or model variants.

Scope
-----
- Applies to runtime experiments that change kernel selection, scheduler configuration, quantization profile, or model variant.
- Intended for mid-to-large scale shadow runs (from single-node to fleet-wide depending on risk).
- Not for synthetic microbenchmarks; this protocol relies on production-shaped traffic.

Objectives
----------
1. Detect regressions in output fidelity (semantic divergence, hallucination rate) introduced by kernel/scheduler/quantization changes.
2. Measure operational impact: latency p50/p95/p99, tail amplification, token cost delta, and memory pressure.
3. Provide clear pass/fail criteria tied to SLOs and risk budgets.
4. Produce automation-friendly artifacts: config snippets, analysis queries, and dashboard templates.

Definitions and terms
---------------------
- Primary cohort: live production serving path receiving real user traffic.
- Shadow cohort: non-responding mirrored path that receives copies of requests for analysis only.
- Stitching: aligning outputs from primary and shadow for token-level and semantic comparison.
- Fidelity delta: measured difference in quality metrics (embedding similarity, logprob delta, downstream evals).
- Cohort window: contiguous time range used for comparison (recommended 60–120 minutes per experiment).

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Experiment owner: eng-serving-runtime feature lead (creates config, runs experiment).
- Observability owner: eng-platform (dashboards, sampling traces).
- Quality owner: applied-ml-and-evals (defines fidelity metrics and acceptance thresholds).
- Oncall / Runbook owner: eng-sre (prepared to abort if operational thresholds are breached).

Pre-requisites
--------------
- Canary availability of shadow cohort image/version with kernel/scheduler/quantization change.
- Traffic mirroring capability at the dispatch layer with request context preservation (headers, timestamps).
- Stable sampling and replay hooks in tracing and KV cache to capture divergent behaviour.
- Baseline corpus of prompts and a lightweight eval harness to run offline checks for severe regressions.

Experiment matrix and cohorts
----------------------------
Use a combinatorial matrix to cover realistic differences:
| Cohort name | Model variant | Kernel set | Quantization | Scheduler profile | Notes |
| Primary | redwood-v1.4 | stable-kernels-1 | q8_compat | standard | baseline production |
| Shadow-A | redwood-v1.4 | new-kernel-optim | q8_compat | standard | tests kernel changes |
| Shadow-B | redwood-v1.4 | new-kernel-optim | q4_ffnx | adjusted-batching | tests quantization + scheduler |
| Shadow-C | redwood-v1.5 | stable-kernels-1 | q8_compat | priority-synth | tests model variant + scheduler |

Sampling strategy
-----------------
- Mirror 100% of a low-risk subset (e.g., read-only assistant queries) for correctness experiments.
- Mirror 5–20% of general traffic with deterministic hashing (request_id mod N) for operational metrics to limit cost.
- Ensure session affinity keys are preserved so session-level KV cache behavior is comparable.

Instrumentation and telemetry
----------------------------
Collect the following per-request:
- request_id, timestamp, cohort_id, model_version, kernel_tag, quant_profile, scheduler_profile
- latency_ms (dispatch, kernel, end-to-end), token_count_in, token_count_out
- model_logprob_sum, per-token logprobs (sampled), response_embedding (128–1024 dim depending on model)
- runtime signals: GPU_util_pct, cuda_mem_free_mb, cpu_load, kvcache_hit_ratio

Metrics and acceptance thresholds
-------------------------------
Quality metrics (primary gates):
- Embedding cosine similarity median ≥ 0.995 and 5th percentile ≥ 0.95 between primary and shadow responses (for single-turn responses).
- Mean per-token logprob delta ≤ 0.15 nats/token across stitched tokens.
- Downstream task AUC / exact-match must not degrade > 1.5% relative.
- Severe hallucination rate (as flagged by eval harness or heuristics) increase ≤ 0.1 percentage point.
Operational metrics (secondary gates):
- delta p99 latency ≤ +12 ms (absolute) OR relative increase ≤ 15% (whichever is smaller).
- p95 latency amplification factor ≤ 1.25.
- Increase in GPU tail stalls > 10% requires immediate abort and triage.
- Token cost delta per 1M tokens ≤ 5% for production budget-sensitive customers.

Procedure: runbook-style steps
-----------------------------
1. Preparation (owner + 2 reviewers):
   - Create experiment config and register cohort IDs in dispatch.
   - Pre-run offline golden-corpus checks (1000 prompts) using the shadow image.
   - Confirm observability dashboards (latency, embeddings, traces) are available.
2. Ramp stage (10–30 minutes):
   - Start mirroring the low-risk hashed subset to shadows at 1% of traffic.
   - Monitor p50/p95/p99, memory, and kvcache heatmap.
   - If operational thresholds breached, pause mirroring and escalate to eng-sre.
3. Validation stage (60–120 minutes):
   - Increase mirror to target sampling rate (5–20%).
   - Persist request/response pairs to stitched storage with retention 14 days for analysis.
   - Run automated fidelity-check jobs every 15 minutes (embedding similarity, LM logprob deltas).
4. Analysis stage (post-run):
   - Aggregate metrics by cohort, request class, model_version, and kernel_tag.
   - Run stratified analysis by sequence length (short/medium/long), session-affinity (cold/warm), and request type.
   - Generate a report with pass/fail and recommended mitigations.
5. Decision & rollout:
   - If all gates pass: prepare canary rollout (10% traffic to new cohort) following standard canary checklist.
   - If any gate fails: create issue with reproduction artifacts and assign to kernel/scheduler owners.

Analysis recipes and queries
---------------------------
- Stitching key: use (request_id || request_timestamp || session_id) to join primary and shadow. If multiple shadow responses exist, align by token offset.
- Example SQL-like aggregation (pseudo):
```
SELECT cohort, percentile(latency_ms, 50) AS p50, percentile(latency_ms, 95) AS p95, 
  avg(embedding_cos_sim) AS mean_emb_sim, percentile(embedding_cos_sim,5) AS emb_sim_p5
FROM stitched_responses
WHERE run_id = 'shadow-2027-02-10'
GROUP BY cohort;
```
- Semantic regression triage: for requests where emb_sim < 0.9, run difference-aware diffing (top-k token alignment + LM delta) and capture the turn-level trace for manual inspection.

Dashboard and reporting templates
--------------------------------
- Live dashboard tiles to prepare: cohort throughput, cohort p50/p95/p99, emb_sim median/p5, lm_logprob_delta distribution, kvcache_hit_ratio, GPU tail stall rate.
- Automated PDF report (generated nightly while experiment runs) with a one-page summary and a detailed appendix containing top 50 low-similarity examples.

Safety and rollback guidelines
----------------------------
- Abort criteria (immediate stop of mirroring): sustained p99 latency increase > 25% OR GPU error rate spike > 3x baseline OR emb_sim cohort median < 0.90.
- Fast rollback: terminate shadow image and clear cohort registration; if changes are in the primary path, execute a canary revert.
- For ambiguous failures, perform a targeted replay of failing requests in isolated environment with full tracing enabled.

Known pitfalls and mitigation notes
----------------------------------
- KV cache non-determinism: session key hashing differences can produce spurious divergence; ensure session-affinity keys are identical across dispatches.
- Sampling bias: avoid mirroring only low-latency traffic; introduce stratified sampling by request type.
- Quantization-induced subtlety: q4 variants can change tokenization margins leading to marginally different token boundaries; stitch by canonicalized token IDs where possible.
- Scheduler preemption effects: high-priority preemption can change runtime ordering and amplify tail latency; include preemption count in telemetry.

Example automation config (dispatch snippet)
-------------------------------------------
```yaml
# shadow cohort registration example
shadow_cohorts:
  - id: shadow-a-kernel-opt
    image: redwood-serving:2027-02-kernel-opt
    mirror_fraction: 0.05 # 5% deterministic via request_id hash
    preserve_headers: ["x-session-id", "x-request-id", "x-original-timestamp"]
    tags: ["kernel_opt", "q8_compat"]
```

Appendix: sample stitched result JSON (single line per request)
--------------------------------------------------------------
```json
{"request_id":"r-123","cohort":"primary","tokens":["Hello","there"],"embedding": [0.001, 0.9, ...],"logprob_sum":-12.4,"latency_ms":34}
```
(When stored, truncate per-token logs for retention; keep full artifacts for the top 500 divergent requests.)

Postmortem and release linkage
-----------------------------
- If this protocol discovers production-impacting regressions, the experiment owner must create a postmortem following the standard incident template and link it to the release notes for the kernel/scheduler/quantization change.
- Include prescriptive mitigations (kernel fallback gating, scheduler guardrails, quantization tuning) and update the rollout playbook.

References and related docs
--------------------------
- Runtime observability contract and telemetry guide (see related_pages).
- Quantization rollout safety playbook.
- Runtime canary and rollout checklist.

Questions and feedback
---------------------
For questions about implementing this protocol, contact the owner team (engineering) or reviewers listed above. Report anomalies to eng-sre via the standard channel with the experiment run_id and top divergent request IDs.
